title: Holy laughter
hookLine: saints often laughed; joy is a fruit of the Spirit
tomorrow: Block close: the shape of a life

cards: Three days ago on this path, Abraham was running to feed three strangers at his tent. Today, stay inside with Sarah, listening behind the door. Outside, one of the visitors is saying that Sarah will have a son.
Genesis is blunt about it: Abraham and Sarah "were old and well stricken in age." So Sarah does the obvious thing. "Sarah laughed within herself."
Quietly. To herself. And the visitor hears it anyway.
"Wherefore did Sarah laugh?" She is afraid. "I laughed not."

teach.b: That first laugh is a hidden one, a laugh of disbelief.

teach.h: ALL THAT HEAR WILL LAUGH WITH ME.
teach.b: Then the promise comes true, and Sarah laughs again, this time out loud and on purpose: "God hath made me to laugh, so that all that hear will laugh with me."
The boy is named Isaac, and readers of the Hebrew hear laughter in the name, as this path did on day three hundred fifty-five.

The story moves from a laugh behind a door to a laugh the whole neighborhood is invited to share. The Bible keeps a place for that second kind. Ecclesiastes says there is "a time to weep, and a time to laugh."

A psalm about coming home from exile says: "Then was our mouth filled with laughter, and our tongue with singing." And Jesus, in Luke, makes it a promise: "Blessed are ye that weep now: for ye shall laugh."

teach.h: THE FRUIT OF THE SPIRIT IS JOY.
teach.b: Paul names joy as part of what grows in a life where God is at work: "the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace." Joy, in second place.
And Christian memory keeps laughing saints. Tradition says that Lawrence, a deacon of Rome, was put to death on a gridiron and joked with his executioners: turn me over, this side is done.
Orthodox Christians honor holy fools, who took Paul's words "we are fools for Christ's sake" at face value. None of this laughs at faith. It's laughter that comes from it.
Solemn and holy aren't the same word.

how: Christians count joy among the fruit of the Spirit; laughter and celebration are part of church life at weddings, baptisms, feasts and fellowship meals, and some traditions tell stories of saints known for their humor.

o: jokes about the Bible told to make church fun
polite smiles kept for solemn religious services
joy that comes from faith, not laughing at faith

p: all that hear will laugh with me
ye that weep now ... shall laugh

s: in Genesis, Sarah laughs only once
she laughs to herself in disbelief, then later: "God hath made me to laugh, so that all that hear will laugh with me."
joy is named among the fruit of the Spirit
"the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace."
Jesus promises laughter to people who weep now
"blessed are ye that weep now: for ye shall laugh."

games.q: you're Sarah. you laughed quietly behind the tent door, and the visitor asks why you laughed. what do you say?
o: walk out and argue with him.
games.why: she denies it, because she was afraid. "nay; but thou didst laugh." no punishment follows; later she laughs out loud and invites everyone to laugh with her.

practice: Bring back a time you laughed until it hurt: who was there, what set it off, the room, the faces, the moment it tipped over. If a smile comes, let it, and if a real laugh comes, let that come too; nobody's grading this.
If you pray, you can give thanks for the joy, and for the people you laughed with.

wordCard.voice: Holy laughter. Joy that comes from faith, not at its expense: Sarah's laugh shared with everyone who hears, and joy named among the fruit of the Spirit.

orig.note: Hebrew, Genesis 21:6: laughter. "God hath made me to laugh."

carryVoice: Your line: joy is holy. Laughter can come from faith, not at its expense. Rest well.
